newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails "historic" U.S. budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails "historic" U.S. budget deal.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday called the budget deal reached with congressional leaders an historic agreement that would help keep the economy growing and benefit generations of Americans.

"We have the pleasure of announcing today an historic agreement that will benefit generations of Americans," Clinton said at a White House ceremony announcing the deal reached on Monday night with the Republican-controlled Congress.

Clinton, surrounded by members of Congress, said the budget legislation, which calls for some $90 billion in net tax cuts over five years, was put together in a way that "honors our values, invests in our people and cuts tax for middle class families".
"After decades of deficits we have put America's fiscal house in order again," Clinton said.
He said the budget deal would help ensure conditions for continued economic prosperity by keeping interest rates down and spurring investment.
The plan, which seeks to balance the budget by 2002, includes a $500-per-child tax credit and a reduction in capital gains taxes to 20 percent from 28 percent.

"This is a balanced budget that honours our commitment to our parents by extending the Medicare trust fund for a decade and into the next generations by continuing our commitment to the environment...," Clinton said.
"We are determined never again to repeat the mistakes of the past when we mortgaged our economy to reckless policy."
